name: Top Result
oneLiner: Google's visual language: white space, Roboto Flex, four thin color accents and a sample results page.
concept:
The buyer already spends the working day inside Google's surfaces: Ads, Analytics, Search Console, the Ad Grants policy pages. Top Result meets them there. The page is pure white, type-led and airy in the Material idiom: Roboto Flex set heavy and slightly wide for headlines, Roboto for reading, Roboto Mono for figures, 8px radii, pill buttons, one hairline gray and one action blue. Google's four colors appear only as thin marks (a four-band underline on the headline's key phrase, four dots as bullet markers, a loading-bar line for the 5% floor), so the site borrows the familiarity of Google's products without ever wearing Google's logo.

The hero object is what the money buys: a sample search results page drawn in CSS, a nonprofit's ad at the top under a Sponsored label with a headline and two sitelinks, and a SAMPLE chip so nobody mistakes it for a client's account. For a tired executive director that picture answers 'what do we actually get?' in one glance; the four figures and the floor line answer 'how do we keep it?'. The register is a product page: calm, clean and competent, forwardable to a board without a covering note.
distinctFrom: It is the only direction on pure white that speaks Material (Roboto Flex, pill buttons, one card elevation) with Google's four colors as hairline accents and the search results page itself as the hero object; Public Works is flat civic-blue blocks with thick rules and a form, Broadsheet is newsprint serif, and none of the others draws the product.
bullets: Pure white, Roboto Flex headlines, Material softness: 8px radii, pill buttons.
Google's four colors as one underline, four dots and one loading bar.
The hero is the product: a sample results page, ad on top.
rightFor: A client who wants the site to feel like the Google products its buyers already trust, and will fund a brand-guideline review.
needs: Legal review of the four-color palette
Sign off the sample nonprofit name
Approve Roboto Flex as the wordmark

palette.note: Pure white, the page ground everywhere and the only ground. Sections are separated by 1px hairlines and one card elevation, never by tinted bands; the CTA band near the footer is the one exception at #F8F9FA.
Google's near-black for headlines, body, the Sponsored label, the floor tick, the mark's mouth and the menu icon. 16.1:1 on white, 14.5:1 on the chip gray.
Captions, the eyebrow, nav links at rest, figure labels, the sample URL and the floor note. 6.05:1 on white and 5.4:1 on #F1F3F4, so it passes AA with margin at the 11px floor.

1px rules under the nav and above the trust strip, the search field's border, the floor panel's frame, dividers between figures and inside the results mock. Chips, skeleton bars and the progress track use #F1F3F4; hover washes use #F8F9FA; skeleton titles #E8EAED.

The one working color: the pill CTA with white type, text buttons, the active nav indicator, the focus ring, the ad headline and sitelinks inside the mock, the cone of the megaphone mark. 4.5:1 on white, which passes AA for normal text with no margin, so it is never lightened and never set on gray. Hover and pressed #174EA6 (7.8:1 on white); tint #E8F0FE for avatars, the sample favicon and the text-button hover wash, with #174EA6 on it at 6.8:1.
First band of every four-color mark. Rules, dots and bars only, never text, never a fill. 3.6:1 on white as a graphic.
Second band. 3.9:1 on white; fails AA as text, so it is never a text color and never an error color (errors use ink and a hairline).

Third band. 1.7:1 on white, which is why no four-color mark carries meaning on its own: the 5% floor is marked by an ink tick and a mono label, the bullets by list semantics, the key phrase by its words.
Fourth band. 3.1:1 on white as a graphic, fails as text; never a success color for copy or a checkmark.

typography.display: Roboto Flex (Google Fonts), the variable family with opsz 8..144, wdth 25..151 and wght 100..1000. Headlines are set at wght 800 with the width axis at 108 via font-variation-settings, optical size automatic, so the h1 is heavy and slightly wide while the same family at wght 600, wdth 100 sets the wordmark and, at wght 700, wdth 104, the h2s. Never italic; emphasis is the four-color underline or weight 500 in Roboto.
typography.body: Roboto (Google Fonts) 400/500/700 for body, nav, buttons, chips, captions, the dot list, the endorsement and every line inside the results mock. 18px/1.5 for the hero sub, 17px/1.55 for body, 16px on the phone.
typography.mono: Roboto Mono (Google Fonts) 400/500 for figures only: the eyebrow's $10,000, the four trust-strip numbers, the CTR readout and the 0 / 5% floor / 10% ticks on the floor line, and dates, account IDs and utilisation figures in reports. It marks 'this is data', so it never sets a sentence.
typography.scaleNotes: h1 60px / 1.04 / -0.022em, Roboto Flex wght 800 wdth 108, two lines ('Show up first.' / 'Stay there.') with the 6px four-band underline under the second, rounded 3px, inset 2px from the glyphs and sitting 2px clear of the descenders; 38px / 1.06 at wdth 104 on phones with a 5px underline. h2 40px / 1.1 / -0.02em wght 700 wdth 104. h3 24px / 1.25 wght 600. Wordmark 20px Roboto Flex 600 (17px phone), -0.01em. Eyebrow 14px Roboto 500 in secondary gray with the dollar figure in 14.5px Roboto Mono 500 ink (13px / 13.5px phone). Hero sub 18px / 1.5, max 520px; body 17px / 1.55, max 68ch. Dot list 15.5px / 1.45 with 9px dots. Buttons 15.5px / 500 in a 48px pill with 26px side padding; the nav pill is 40px at 14px, the phone nav pill 36px at 14px; text buttons match the primary size in action blue with an 18px arrow. Endorsement 15.5px / 1.45 with a 13px attribution. Trust figures 28px Roboto Mono 500, -0.02em, with the '+' as a 14px superscript in gray and 'of' at 16px; 26px on phones; labels 13.5px gray. Inside the results mock: query 15.5px ink, SAMPLE chip 11px / 500 / +0.06em uppercase, hint 12.5px gray, Sponsored 13px / 700 ink, advertiser 14px / 500, URL 12.5px gray, ad headline 19px action blue, description 14px / 1.45 ink, sitelinks 14px / 500 blue with 12.5px gray descriptors; on the phone the headline is 17px and everything else steps down 0.5px. Floor panel: title 14px / 500, readout 13px mono, ticks 11px mono, note 13.5px gray. Radii: 24px pills, 22px search field, 8px cards and panels, 4px chips, 3px four-color marks, 50% avatars. Elevation: one level only, Material's 0 1px 2px rgba(60,64,67,.3) + 0 1px 3px 1px rgba(60,64,67,.15), on the results card; every other edge is a hairline.

layout:
- Grid and rhythm: 12 columns, 1200px container, 24px gutters, 48px side margins (16px on phones), 8px base spacing. Structure is drawn with 1px #DADCE0 hairlines and white space, not bands; the only elevation is the results card. A four-color budget of three marks per viewport (underline, dots, floor bar in the hero) is written into the style guide so the accents stay thin. Accessibility contract shared with the other directions: 48px primary targets, 3px action-blue focus ring with a 3px offset, 18px hero sub, AA at every size, CSS-only reveals.
- 0. Nav (64px, hairline beneath). The megaphone mark redrawn in action blue and ink, wordmark 'Nonprofit Megaphone' in Roboto Flex 600. Links Ad Grant, Services, Case studies, Guides, Team, Pricing in Roboto 500 gray; the active link is action blue with a 3px Material tab indicator. Right: 'Client sign-in' as a text button (the login that signals a real product behind the sales page) and the 40px 'Book a free call' pill, the same blue as the hero pill so the action color is learned once.
- 1. Hero (6/6, 36px above, 32px below, 826px page total in the mockup). Lead: eyebrow with '$10,000' in Roboto Mono, then 'a month in Google search ads, free to eligible nonprofits'; h1 'Show up first. / Stay there.' with the four-band underline under 'Stay there.'; 18px sub; a four-item list whose markers are the four dots (100% acquisition guarantee in writing; one of nine inaugural Google Ad Grants Certified Professional agencies; a named team of 60+ reporting monthly; the $25 meet-the-CEO promise); the 48px 'Book a free call' pill beside the 'Am I eligible?' text button and '4 questions, no email'; under a hairline, the Michelle Hurtado endorsement as a Material list item with a circular avatar. Demo column: the results card (SAMPLE chip and 'Your ad, at the top of the results page' hint; a rounded search field with a magnifier and the query 'free family counseling near me'; the ad block: Sponsored, a favicon disc and 'Willow Creek Family Services / willowcreekfamily.org', the headline 'Free Family Counseling | Same-Week Appointments' in action blue, a two-line description, two sitelinks with descriptors; then one neutral skeleton result so the rest of the page is suggested, not copied) with a caption stating it is a sample and not a client's account; beneath it the floor panel: 'The rule Google enforces' with 'CTR >= 5.0%' in mono, the four-color loading bar filled to the 5% tick on a 0-10% track, and the two-months-then-deactivation sentence.
- 2. Trust strip (hairline above, ~115px). Four figures in Roboto Mono between vertical hairline dividers (780+ nonprofits under management, $48M+ in Google Ads managed, 100% approval guaranteed in writing, 1 of 9 inaugural Google-certified agencies), then 'Clients include' and eight plain-text names (UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, Solar Sister, AAU, JFCS) separated by 3px dots. Static, no carousel, no logos until licences are in hand.
- 3. '01 How it works' (4 up). Four hairline cards, each opened by one of the four dots in sequence: Apply (we get the account approved, guaranteed), Build (keywords, ads, conversion tracking), Keep (above the 5% floor, inside the policy), Report (a named lead, every month). The one place the four dots appear below the hero.
- 4. '02 The rules' (full width). A Material data table: Requirement / What Google does if you miss it / What we do about it, one row each for the $10,000 monthly cap, the 5% CTR floor and two-month deactivation, mandatory conversion tracking, the keyword quality rules and the annual programme survey, with the policy page cited and dated in each row.
- 5. '03 Am I eligible?' (7/5). Four questions as Material choice chips with a hairline progress rule, honest end states for hospitals, schools and government entities, no email required; the end card offers the call.
- 6. '04 The account, every month' (5/7). Left: the account lead's one-sentence monthly note as a list item with a circular portrait, client, month, dated and signed, rotating from the CMS. Right: a real monthly report rendered as a Material card: utilisation against the $10,000 cap as a hairline meter, CTR against the floor line drawn with the same ink tick, compliance checks, conversions, with a visible REDACTED chip on anything withheld and a 'Forward to board' PDF action.
- 7. '05 Case studies' (4/4/4). Three cards with a fixed KPI trio in Roboto Mono (CTR, conversion rate, outcome per month), before and after, a named quote, and a link to the full filterable table.
- 8. '06 What it costs' (7/5). The management fee range as a Material price list, the 100% acquisition guarantee as a clause, the $25 meet-the-CEO promise with Amber Snow's name and plain-text email. This is the nav's 'Pricing' anchor.
- 9. '07 Other services'. A hairline-divided seven-row list (Ad Grant, Content, SEO, VisitorEmail, Remarketing, Microsoft Ads, Spanish Ad Creation) with one-line descriptions; Material Symbols Outlined at 24px where an icon helps, never illustrations.
- 10. '08 The people on your account'. Circular portraits in a dense 6-up grid with 'Nonprofits I support' captions naming real clients, the retreat candid as a full-width 8px-radius plate with a credit line, and the credentials line (Google Ad Grants Certified, inaugural cohort; Google Partner; Inc. 5000, four years).
- 11. '09 Guides' (5/7). The ungated Ad Grants guide as a featured card with reading time and a last-reviewed date; the latest three posts with dates and bylines.
- 12. CTA band on #F8F9FA between two hairlines: one headline in Roboto Flex, one blue pill, one line of small print with the phone number, 'Am I eligible?' and Amber's email.
- 13. Footer on white: four hairline-divided columns, the real Beaverton, OR address, the Google Partner badge on its own white space per the badge rules, 'Client sign-in', the newsletter field as a rounded Material text field, and the line 'Nonprofit Megaphone is an independent agency and is not affiliated with Google LLC', which the trademark guidance makes non-negotiable.
imagery: No illustration system and no stock. The site's pictures are its product's own surfaces, drawn as UI: the sample results page in the hero, the monthly report as a Material card, the rules table, the eligibility chips. Each is typeset in HTML with hairlines, 8px radii and Roboto, so it reads as a product screenshot without being one. Anything that represents a real account carries a visible REDACTED chip; anything invented carries the SAMPLE chip in the same 11px uppercase style, in the mockup and in production. Photography is content, not palette: NPM's people in natural light with a neutral grade, cropped as circular Material avatars (40px in list items, 96px in the team grid) and the retreat candid as a rectangular 8px-radius plate with a credit line; beneficiary photography supplied by clients, dignity-first and consented, used sparingly. Iconography is Material Symbols Outlined (served from Google Fonts) at 20px and 24px, weight 400, in ink or secondary gray, plus the megaphone mark redrawn as true vector in action blue and ink; the mockups use inline SVG for the magnifier, arrow and menu so they are self-contained. The four colors never touch a photograph, an icon or the mark: they exist only as the underline, the dots and the floor bar, at most three marks per viewport, and never adjacent to the word 'Google'. Client marks are plain-text names in Roboto 500 gray; licensed monochrome logos may replace them one at a time where recognition matters.
motion: Motion is Material's: short, standard-eased (cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)), functional, and always complete without it. Three CSS-only devices in the hero, each with its resting state as the natural style and a single 'from' keyframe: the four-band underline draws left to right under 'Stay there.' (scaleX, 700ms, 250ms delay); the results card rises 10px and fades in (600ms, 100ms delay); the floor bar fills from 0 to the 5% tick in its four bands (900ms, 300ms delay), so the loading-bar metaphor plays once and then holds. Hover: the primary pill darkens to #174EA6 with no lift and no shadow; text buttons take the #E8F0FE wash with #174EA6 type and their arrow moves 3px; nav links take the #F8F9FA wash, the active one switching to #174EA6 so blue never sits on gray at 4.5:1; ad headline and sitelinks underline. Focus appears instantly. Below the hero, GSAP (free in Webflow) may add two devices, both static-first: trust figures count up in tabular mono on first view (900ms) and the report card's meter fills on scroll-enter; headlines and body do not animate. prefers-reduced-motion: every animation and transition is disabled and each device rests at its final state, which the mockups implement with a single media query. No parallax, no Lottie, no marquee, no carousel; the client roll is static.
mobile: The 390px hero is a single column with the order fixed in CSS: a 56px nav (mark + wordmark at 17px, a 36px 'Book a call' pill, a 44px round menu target that hangs 10px into the gutter) under a hairline; a one-line eyebrow with the mono figure; the h1 at 38px / 1.06 (wdth 104) on two lines with the 5px underline; the sub at 16px (four lines); a full-width 48px 'Book a free call' pill whose top sits at 326px; the 'Am I eligible?' text button (44px tall, 380-424px) with '4 questions, no email' beside it, all inside a 760px fold. The results card follows at 440px so its SAMPLE chip, search field and Sponsored label sit above the fold: it is condensed to the field (40px), the ad block with the headline at 17px and two-column sitelinks, and one skeleton result, then a two-line caption. The single trust element is the figures card: a 2 x 2 hairline grid of the four figures in Roboto Mono at 26px (780+, $48M+, 100%, 1 of 9) with, in its foot, the floor panel (title, mono readout, the four-color loading bar to the 5% tick, one sentence). The page runs to about 1220px and scrolls; the Hurtado endorsement, the dot list and the client roll move below the fold into section 01 on phones. Key sections on phone: the rules table becomes stacked hairline entries with the three headings as labels; the monthly note and report stack 1/1 with the note first; case-study cards stack with the KPI trio as a 3-up strip; the team grid is 3-up circular avatars. Labels floor at 11px (the SAMPLE chip and the mono ticks); secondary gray holds AA on white and on the chip gray.
a11y: WCAG 2.2 AA is the target at every size and most pairs clear AAA. Measured on the actual grounds: ink #202124 on white 16.1:1 and on #F1F3F4 14.5:1; secondary #5F6368 on white 6.05:1 and on #F1F3F4 5.4:1, so 11px labels pass AA with margin; action blue #1A73E8 on white 4.5:1 (normal text passes, with no margin, so the token is locked and never appears on gray); white on #1A73E8 4.5:1 for 15.5px/500 button type; hover #174EA6 7.8:1 on white and white on it 7.8:1; #174EA6 on the #E8F0FE tint 6.8:1 and on the #F8F9FA wash 7.4:1, which is why text buttons and the active nav link switch to #174EA6 on hover (#1A73E8 on those washes would be 3.9:1 and 4.3:1). The four colors are never text: #FBBC04 is 1.7:1 and #34A853 3.1:1 on white, #EA4335 3.9:1, #4285F4 3.6:1, so they fail as text and yellow fails even as a UI graphic, which is why no four-color mark carries meaning on its own: the floor is marked by an ink tick (16:1) and a mono label, the bullets by list semantics, the key phrase by its words. Smallest text is 11px (the SAMPLE chip and the bar ticks); hero sub 18px, body 17px, phone body 16px. Focus: a 3px #1A73E8 outline with 3px offset on every link and button (:focus-visible), which shows as a ring with a white gap around the blue pill. Targets: 48px pills and text buttons, 44px menu and eligibility targets on the phone, a 40px nav pill with 12px clearance. Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion. Text equivalents: the results mock is a figure labelled 'Sample search results page' with its caption stating it is not a client's account, the search field is role=img with the query as its label, the floor panel a labelled group, the floor bar is role=img with a label stating the scale and the 5% floor, the favicon disc, avatar initials, skeleton bars, four-color bands and the mark are aria-hidden. Landmarks: nav labelled Primary, hero labelled by the h1, the trust strip a labelled region. Color is never the only carrier of meaning: the active nav link has an indicator bar as well as blue, links inside the mock underline on hover and sit in a labelled ad block, and the floor line is labelled in words.

heroCopy.eyebrow: $10,000 a month in Google search ads, free to eligible nonprofits
heroCopy.headline: Show up first. Stay there.
heroCopy.sub: Google gives eligible nonprofits $10,000 a month in search ads. Nonprofit Megaphone gets the account approved, keeps it above Google's 5% click-through floor, and reports every month.

signatureMoments: The sample results page as the hero object: a rounded search field, a Sponsored ad for a fictional nonprofit with a headline and two sitelinks, a SAMPLE chip and one skeleton result, in a Material card with the site's only elevation, so the first viewport shows the buyer exactly what $10,000 a month buys without a logo, a screenshot or a claim about a real client.

'Show up first. / Stay there.' in Roboto Flex at wght 800 and wdth 108, with the four-band underline drawing in under 'Stay there.': the whole promise (be at the top, keep the account) in five words, and the four colors used once, thinly, on the phrase about retention.

Google's 5% floor as a loading bar: a 0-10% track with the four bands filling to an ink tick labelled '5% floor' in Roboto Mono, the readout 'CTR >= 5.0%' beside the title, and the two-months-then-deactivation rule in one sentence, so the rule the buyer fears is drawn in the idiom of a progress indicator rather than a warning.

Four dots as bullet markers: the guarantee, the certification, the named team and the $25 promise each opened by one Google color, the only other place the four colors appear on the page, with a written budget of three four-color marks per viewport.

The trust strip as a Material list: four figures in Roboto Mono between hairline dividers with the '+' as a gray superscript, then 'Clients include' and eight plain-text names, so proof reads as data and a roll rather than a badge wall.
dependencies: A legal and brand-guideline review of the palette before build, as a client decision: Google's brand guidelines restrict third parties from using the Google logo, wordmark and the four-color combination in ways that imply endorsement. The direction never uses the logo or sets the word 'Google' in the four colors and keeps the colors to thin marks, but the client must confirm that use with counsel; the fallback (underline, dots and bar in action blue and ink) is designed and costed.

Sign off the sample: 'Willow Creek Family Services', its URL and ad copy are fictional and must be checked against real organisations before publishing, or replaced by a consenting client's real ad with a REDACTED chip on anything withheld.

Wordmark and mark: agree the wordmark reset to Roboto Flex 600 and the mark's blue moving from the current brand blue to #1A73E8, positioned to 780 existing clients as a sharpening; confirm the Google Partner badge placement rules for the footer.

Font delivery: Roboto Flex with opsz, wdth and wght is a large variable file from Google Fonts; production self-hosts a subset of the three axes (or accepts Google Fonts hosting and its privacy note), and the Webflow class set locks wght 800 / wdth 108 for the h1 so editors cannot soften it.

CMS fields for the four figures with a last-updated date, a consented real monthly report for section 04, and a named account lead per client for the monthly note; the trust strip must never be hand-edited.
risks: Trademark and endorsement: even as accents, four colors next to the word 'Google' on a page about a Google programme could be read as implied endorsement. Mitigations are built in (no logo, no four-color wordmark, a three-mark budget, the 'independent agency, not affiliated with Google LLC' footer line) but the palette is a legal call the client makes before build; if counsel says no, the direction survives in blue and ink and loses its signature.

Looking like Google cuts both ways: the page could be mistaken for a Google property, or read as generic Material. The counterweights are the NPM mark and wordmark first in the nav, the results mock labelled SAMPLE, real figures in mono, Amber Snow's $25 promise and the Hurtado endorsement as human objects; cutting them leaves a template.

Contrast has no slack: #1A73E8 on white is 4.5:1 exactly, so any tinted ground under blue text, any lighter blue, or an editor adding a green success line or a yellow highlight breaks AA immediately. The token set and locked classes are load-bearing.

The phone page is long (about 1220px) because the results card and the figures card both earn their place; the contract (CTA at 326px, eligibility link at 380px, the card's top 320px above a 760px fold) is in the mobile mockup and must be prototyped in Webflow, not assumed.
references: Material Design 3 guidelines (m3.material.io) for the type scale, elevation levels, pill buttons, hairline dividers and choice chips
Google Workspace and Google Store product pages for white, type-led heroes where the product's own UI is the image
The Roboto Flex specimen (Google Fonts and Font Bureau) for the heavy, wide display setting and the wdth axis
Google Ads Help's 'anatomy of a search ad' diagrams for the ad block, with the logo and page furniture removed and a SAMPLE label added
Google for Nonprofits and Google Ad Grants help pages as the register the buyers already read every month
